canonical_name: libDAI (0.3 line, 2012 mirror) -- a C++ library of approximate inference on factor graphs: (loopy) belief propagation, junction tree, mean field, TreeEP, Gibbs, and more (Joris Mooij)
lineage: Pearl's belief propagation (1982/1988) and its loopy generalisation, exact junction-tree inference, and a dozen approximate methods, in one reference library (JMLR MLOSS 2010) with the standard examples (sprinkler network) and unit tests. The canonical open BELIEF-PROPAGATION implementation; the vault's ldpc-codes does BP only for decoding.
version: github.com/dbtsai/libDAI master (a 2012 mirror of the libdai.org 0.3 line; exact version from ChangeLog in the tree; commit in hashes)
compiler_or_interpreter: g++ 12 (docker bookworm) with libboost-dev, libgmp-dev, libgmpxx (apt at run time, recorded)
entry_points: examples/example_sprinkler.cpp (exact + BP marginals on the sprinkler network); tests/testdai; examples/example.cpp with a .fg factor graph

example.output: P(Sprinkler|WetGrass) etc. by exact inference and by BP -- BP equals exact on this tree (the ORACLE)

upstream_docs: Mooij, libDAI: A Free and Open Source C++ Library for Discrete Approximate Inference in Graphical Models, JMLR 11, 2010
Pearl, Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems, 1988

human_capability_summary.built_to: compute marginals and MAP states on graphical models by passing messages along factor-graph edges, exactly on trees and approximately on loopy graphs
human_capability_summary.pressure: exact inference is exponential on loopy graphs; loopy BP may not converge
human_capability_summary.success_means: on a tree, BP marginals equal the exact ones; on loopy graphs, convergence and accuracy are reported

human_failure_condition: loopy BP oscillates or converges to wrong marginals
behavioral_entry_point: run BP on a loopy .fg (tests/ ships several) with different damping/update schedules and record convergence

lineage_relations.note: BP as a decoder vs BP as a general inference engine
